brief: Zero Hedge recaps a week in which midterm election results handed governorships covering roughly 45% of planned US data-center capacity to anti-buildout candidates, triggering a Nasdaq rout, a record Cboe put day, a hedge-fund round-trip of 2026 gains and Microsoft's cancellation of its Oracle AI rental. Against that backdrop, Goldman published two bullish notes arguing the construction cycle survives: 86GW is already under construction backing a roughly $900bn high-confidence pipeline (up to $1.9tn including lower-probability projects), construction spending growth hit 90% YoY in September, and under-construction/high-probability capacity alone covers Goldman's 2027-28 capacity forecasts. Goldman's Adam Bubes raised 2026-2028 construction-spending forecasts (to $80bn, $100bn and a new $125bn) and argues the midterm-driven moratoriums shift spending timing rather than cut the total addressable market, since the pipeline was already running ahead of historical build-out pace before the election. Texas is 26% of 2026-30 net capacity additions, and its moratorium's length is tied by Wells Fargo to the state legislature's January-May 2027 session. The author sides with the optimists on the TAM question but flags debt-financing risk to delayed, levered developers as the real fault line.
